text:
Sam W: quick summary from a 10k bring-up for varnish14 (14B) comparing int4->int6 mixed quant strategy. main idea: use a lightweight confidence-head classifier to trigger fallbacks to int6 or rerank only for low-confidence outputs. yields most cost upside while keeping hallucination in check. details below.

Priya R: ooh, confidence head? paste top-line numbers pls.

Sam W: eval snapshot (auto): sample_n=10000, baseline=int6, alt=int4+confhead, cost_delta=-36% (per-token), qa_acc_delta=-0.9pp, hallucination_delta=+0.9pp, p95_latency_delta=-6ms for int4 main + +18ms when confhead triggers int6 fallback, conf_trigger_rate=11%

Noah K: that looks promising. what's the raw table?

Sam W: table:
```
variant                 cost_per_1k  QA_acc  halluc_rate  p95_latency
varnish14-int6          $0.95        84.4%   2.6%         240ms
varnish14-int4+conf     $0.61        83.5%   3.5%         234ms (base) / 252ms (when fallback applies)
```

Priya R: so effective cost is lower even with ~11% triggering to int6. what's the overall effective cost per 1k in sim?

Sam W: effective cost_per_1k ~= $0.68 assuming conf_trigger_rate=11% and rerank_on_fallback=false. If we enable rerank for fallback outputs cost_per_1k -> $0.72 but hallucination drops ~1.4pp on fallback slice.

Lina: where are quality regressions concentrated? long summaries again?

Sam W: majority on abstractive summarization and multi-turn long-dialog threads with high template drift. QA and code tasks are near-parity (<0.3pp). confidence-head triggers align well with true failures (~78% precision @ that threshold).

Noah K: what's the confidence head model? cheap logistic on pooled CLS-like head?

Sam W: simple linear classifier on last-layer pooled norm + kelvin-calibrated softmax features. lightweight (~2-3ms inference) co-deployed on the same runtime. we also ran a calibration-scan to pick threshold targeting ~10-12% trigger rate.

Priya R: product ask: recommended rollout + unit econ for GTN?

Sam W: proposal: soft-launch int4+confhead for cost-sensitive endpoints with fallback to int6 when conf low. Canary 3% -> 20% over 10 days. Gate on: overall hallucination_rate, conf_trigger_rate, QA-slice delta, and p95 latency.

Sam W: unit-econ quick numbers (assume avg tokens/req=1.6k):
- baseline all-int6: cost_per_1k=$0.95 -> cost_per_req ~= $1.52 -> per_1M_req ~= $1,520
- conf-hybrid (11% fallback): effective cost_per_1k~$0.68 -> cost_per_req ~= $1.09 -> per_1M_req ~= $1,090
- savings ~= $430 per 1M reqs (~28.3%)

Lina: callout: these savings assume our prompt priming stays constant. adding heavy system prompts inflates token counts and reduces % savings. also note extra operational complexity (confhead threshold tuning).

Noah K: sim command we used:
```bash
python tools/sim_confhead.py --trace traces/longmix_10k.json \
  --model_variant "varnish14-int4+conf" \
  --conf_threshold 0.42 \
  --metrics cost,qa_acc,halluc_rate,trigger_rate,p95 \
  --out reports/varnish14_conf_3712345678.json
```

Priya R: mitigation options if hallucination creeps up during canary?

Sam W: options: tighten conf threshold (lower trigger rate), enable reranker on fallback outputs, or route >2k token contexts to int6 by policy. Reranker recovers most regression but adds ~6% unit cost.

ops-bot: note: please add billing tag `variant=varnish14-int4-conf` and `feature=conf-fallback` for canary traffic; recommended alert: hallucination_rate > 4% for 10m OR conf_trigger_rate > 20% sustained 5m.

Priya R: can someone draft a one-paragraph exec blurb for GTN?

Sam W: draft: "Recommend a cautious hybrid: use int4 as the cost-default with a lightweight confidence classifier that routes low-confidence outputs to int6. In simulations this reduced model spend by ~28% while keeping QA and hallucination within product guardrails. Start with a 3% canary and expand to 20% over 10 days with gates on hallucination, trigger rate, QA-slice regressions, and p95 latency. If hallucination exceeds 4% or triggers spike above 20%, revert routing to all-int6 and run a short investigation."
